title: Reproduction in Lower and Higher Animals
subject: Biology
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET / NEET • Quick Revision

nodes.title: Asexual Reproduction & Regeneration in Animals
points: Asexual reproduction in animals: Occurs without formation or fusion of gametes, producing genetically identical clones.

Gemmule formation (Internal budding in freshwater sponges e.g. Spongilla): Aggregation of dormant totipotent archaeocytes enclosed by thick protective membrane reinforced by amphidisc siliceous spicules; germinate upon return of favorable conditions.
External Budding: In Hydra, outgrowth develops on parent body due to repeated mitotic cell division at specific site; matures, detaches, and lives as an independent individual.

Regeneration: Morphallaxis (reorganization of remaining tissue) and Epimorphosis (replacement of lost parts by dedifferentiation and proliferation); Planaria exhibits phenomenal true regeneration with morphological polarity.

formulas.label: Gemmule structure components
formulas.expr: Archaeocytes (totipotent cells) + Internal/External membrane + Amphidisc spicules + Micropyle

formulas.label: Animal asexual modes matching
formulas.expr: Spongilla = Gemmule | Hydra = Budding | Planaria = True Regeneration

nodes.title: Male Reproductive System & Histology of Testis
points: Scrotum: Thermoregulatory pouch holding testes outside abdominal cavity at 2 to 2.5 °C below core body temperature (essential for spermatogenesis).
Testis histology: Covered by fibrous tunica albuginea; contains 200-300 lobules, each with 1-4 highly coiled Seminiferous Tubules.

Cells of Seminiferous tubules: 1) Spermatogenic cells (spermatogonia undergoing meiosis); 2) Sertoli cells (Nurse cells: provide mechanical support, nourishment to sperms, secrete Inhibin to inhibit FSH, secrete ABP to concentrate testosterone, form blood-testis barrier).
Interstitial / Leydig cells: Located in connective tissue between tubules; synthesize and secrete androgens (Testosterone) under stimulation of LH (ICSH).

Duct pathway & Accessory glands: Seminiferous tubules → Rete testis → Vasa efferentia → Epididymis (sperm maturation & storage) → Vas deferens → Ejaculatory duct → Urethra. Glands: Seminal vesicles (60% semen; fructose, prostaglandins, clotting proteins), Prostate gland (30%; alkaline, citric acid, acid phosphatase), Bulbourethral / Cowper's glands (alkaline lubricant).

formulas.label: Pathway of sperm transit
formulas.expr: Seminiferous tubules → Rete testis → Vasa efferentia → Epididymis → Vas deferens → Ejaculatory duct → Urethra

formulas.label: Semen composition fractions
formulas.expr: Seminal vesicles (60%) + Prostate gland (30%) + Bulbourethral glands & Spermatozoa (10%)

nodes.title: Female Reproductive System & Histology of Ovary
points: Ovary anatomy: Paired primary sex organs in pelvic cavity; covered by germinal epithelium, outer cellular cortex (containing ovarian follicles in various stages), and inner vascular medulla.
Follicular progression: Primordial follicle → Primary follicle → Secondary follicle → Tertiary follicle (antrum filled with liquor folliculi) → Mature Graafian follicle.

Mature Graafian follicle structure: Contains Secondary Oocyte arrested at Metaphase II; surrounded by non-cellular glycoprotein Zona pellucida, cellular Corona radiata (radially elongated granulosa cells), and Cumulus oophorus.

Fallopian tubes (Oviducts, 10-12 cm): 1) Infundibulum with finger-like fimbriae (collects ovulated oocyte); 2) Ampulla (longest, widest portion, SITE OF FERTILIZATION); 3) Isthmus (short, narrow part opening into uterus).

Uterus (Womb) wall layers: Perimetrium (outer serous), Myometrium (thick middle smooth muscle, oxytocin-induced labor contractions), Endometrium (inner glandular vascular, undergoes cyclic changes during menstruation).

formulas.label: Graafian follicle layers (inside to outside)
formulas.expr: Secondary oocyte → Zona pellucida → Corona radiata → Antrum → Theca interna → Theca externa

formulas.label: Fallopian tube segments order
formulas.expr: Fimbriae → Infundibulum → Ampulla (fertilization site) → Isthmus → Uterus

nodes.title: Gametogenesis: Spermatogenesis vs Oogenesis
points: Spermatogenesis: Continuous process starting at puberty in testes. 1) Multiplication phase: Spermatogonia (2n) divide mitotically; 2) Growth phase: Forms Primary spermatocyte (2n); 3) Maturation phase: Meiosis I forms 2 Secondary spermatocytes (n); Meiosis II forms 4 Spermatids (n); 4) Spermiogenesis: Morphological transformation of round spermatids into motile spermatozoa (Acrosome from Golgi, Middle piece mitochondria, Tail from centriole). Yields 4 sperms per primary spermatocyte.

Oogenesis: Discontinuous process initiated during fetal life. 1) Multiplication: Oogonia (2n) formed in fetal ovary (~2 million, none added after birth); 2) Growth: Primary oocytes (2n) enter Meiosis I and arrest at Prophase I (diplotene stage) until puberty; 3) Maturation: Each month, 1 primary oocyte completes Meiosis I yielding large Secondary oocyte (n) + tiny 1st Polar body (n). Arrests at Metaphase II!
Completion of Oogenesis: Penetration of sperm triggers completion of Meiosis II, releasing second polar body and forming functional haploid Ovum (ootid). Yields 1 ovum + 2-3 polar bodies.

formulas.label: Spermatogenesis yield ratio
formulas.expr: 1 Primary Spermatocyte (2n) (Meiosis) → 4 Functional Spermatozoa (n)

formulas.label: Oogenesis yield ratio
formulas.expr: 1 Primary Oocyte (2n) (Meiosis) → 1 Functional Ovum (n) + 2 or 3 Polar bodies (degenerate)

formulas.label: Sperm organelle origins
formulas.expr: Acrosome = Golgi apparatus | Middle piece spiral sheath = Mitochondria (Nebenkern) | Tail axial filament = Centriole

nodes.title: Menstrual Cycle & Hormonal Feedback
points: Menstrual cycle: 28-day reproductive cycle in primate females divided into 4 chronological phases:
1. Menstrual phase (Days 1-5): Breakdown of endometrium and blood vessels due to sharp withdrawal of progesterone and estrogen; discharge of 45-100 mL blood.

2. Follicular / Proliferative phase (Days 6-13): Anterior pituitary FSH stimulates growth of ovarian follicles; growing follicles secrete Estrogen, which stimulates repair and proliferation of endometrium.
3. Ovulatory phase (Day 14): High estrogen triggers positive feedback causing LH Surge (rapid surge in LH). LH surge induces rupture of Graafian follicle and release of secondary oocyte (Ovulation).

4. Luteal / Secretory phase (Days 15-28): Ruptured follicle transforms into Corpus luteum (yellow body) under LH influence; secretes massive amounts of Progesterone to maintain thickened endometrium for implantation. If fertilization does not occur, corpus luteum degenerates into Corpus albicans (white scar), progesterone drops, triggering menstruation.

formulas.label: Menstrual cycle phases & days
formulas.expr: Menstrual (Day 1-5) → Proliferative / Follicular (Day 6-13) → Ovulatory (Day 14) → Secretory / Luteal (Day 15-28)

formulas.label: Key hormonal triggers
formulas.expr: LH Surge at Day 14 → Induces Ovulation | High Progesterone in Luteal phase → Maintains Endometrium

formulas.label: Corpus luteum life cycle
formulas.expr: Ruptured Follicle (LH) → Corpus Luteum (Progesterone) → (no pregnancy) → Corpus Albicans

nodes.title: Fertilization & Early Cleavage: Zygote to Blastocyst
points: Fertilization: Occurs at the ampulla of the Fallopian tube.
1. Capacitation: Physiological conditioning of sperms in female genital tract (~5-6 hours; removal of acrosomal cholesterol/proteins).
2. Acrosomal reaction: Sperm releases Hyaluronidase (dissolves hyaluronic acid cementing corona radiata) and Acrosin / Zona lysin (digests zona pellucida).
3. Cortical & Zona reaction: Sperm entry triggers Ca²⁺ wave; cortical granules exocytose, hardening zona pellucida to establish permanent slow block to Polyspermy (monospermy guaranteed).
Cleavage & Blastulation: Rapid mitotic divisions without growth. Zygote (Day 0) → 2-cell (30 hr) → 4-cell (60 hr) → Morula (16-32 cells, solid mulberry shape, Day 3-4) → Blastocyst (Day 5-6).
Blastocyst structure: Outer Trophoblast (forms fetal placenta), Inner Cell Mass (embryoblast containing pluripotent stem cells), and fluid-filled Blastocoel.
Implantation: Attachment of blastocyst to endometrium around Day 7; trophoblast secretes hCG to maintain corpus luteum.

formulas.label: Cleavage progression timeline
formulas.expr: Zygote (2n, Day 0) → 2-cell (30 hr) → 4-cell (60 hr) → Morula (16-32 cells, Day 3-4) → Blastocyst (Day 5-6) → Implantation (Day 7)

formulas.label: Blastocyst components
formulas.expr: Trophoblast (extraembryonic membranes/placenta) + Inner Cell Mass (Embryo proper) + Blastocoel

formulas.label: Polyspermy prevention mechanisms
formulas.expr: Fast block: Membrane depolarization (−70 mV to +20 mV) | Slow block: Cortical reaction & Zona reaction

nodes.title: Gastrulation, Germ Layers & Organogenesis
points: Gastrulation: Morphogenetic movement and rearrangement of blastomeres forming 3 primary germ layers: Ectoderm, Mesoderm, Endoderm.
Fate of Ectoderm: Epidermis of skin, hair, nails, nervous system (brain, spinal cord, nerves), retina and lens of eye, internal ear, enamel of teeth, adrenal medulla, pituitary gland.

Fate of Mesoderm: Dermis of skin, all muscular tissues, connective tissues, skeletal system (bones, cartilage), circulatory system (heart, blood vessels, blood), kidneys, gonads (testes, ovaries), adrenal cortex.
Fate of Endoderm: Epithelial lining of digestive tract, respiratory tract, urinary bladder, liver, pancreas, thyroid, parathyroid, thymus.

Extra-embryonic membranes: Amnion (amniotic fluid cushions embryo against shock/desiccation), Chorion (forms fetal part of placenta), Allantois (forms umbilical vessels), Yolk sac (early hematopoiesis).
Placenta: Hemochorial; secretes hCG, hPL (human placental lactogen), Estrogen, Progesterone, and Relaxin.

formulas.label: Germ layer origins quick guide
formulas.expr: Ectoderm: Nervous system, skin epidermis | Mesoderm: Muscles, skeleton, heart, kidneys, gonads | Endoderm: Gut lining, liver, pancreas

formulas.label: Placental hormones checklist
formulas.expr: hCG (pregnancy test marker), hPL, Estrogen, Progesterone, Relaxin (secreted by ovary/placenta in late pregnancy)

nodes.title: Parturition, Lactation & Contraceptive Methods
points: Parturition (Birth): Neuroendocrine mechanism triggered by Foetal Ejection Reflex. Fully developed fetus and placenta send signals inducing mild uterine contractions; stimulates maternal posterior pituitary to release Oxytocin (birth hormone), causing vigorous myometrial contractions via positive feedback. Relaxin relaxes pubic symphysis.
Lactation: Prolactin (PRL, anterior pituitary) stimulates milk synthesis; Oxytocin (posterior pituitary) causes milk ejection / let-down reflex by contracting myoepithelial cells.
Colostrum: First yellowish milk secreted for 2-3 days; rich in antibodies (Secretory IgA) providing passive immunity to the newborn.

Contraception: 1) Natural: Periodic abstinence (fertile window Day 10-17), Coitus interruptus, Lactational amenorrhea (up to 6 months); 2) Barrier: Condoms (protect against STDs), Diaphragms; 3) IUDs: Non-medicated (Lippes loop), Copper-releasing (CuT, Cu7, Multiload-375: suppress sperm motility), Hormone-releasing (Progestasert, LNG-20: make uterus unsuitable for implantation); 4) Oral pills: Saheli (Centchroman, non-steroidal once-a-week pill); 5) Permanent: Vasectomy (vas deferens cut/tied) and Tubectomy (fallopian tubes cut/tied); 6) MTP: Safe up to 12 weeks (1st trimester).

formulas.label: Parturition neuroendocrine reflex
formulas.expr: Foetal Ejection Reflex → Hypothalamus → Posterior Pituitary → Oxytocin release → Vigorous Myometrial Contraction

formulas.label: Lactation hormones roles
formulas.expr: Prolactin (PRL) = Milk Synthesis | Oxytocin = Milk Ejection / Let-down reflex

formulas.label: Copper IUD action mechanism
formulas.expr: Releases Cu²⁺ ions → Inhibits sperm motility & suppresses fertilizing capacity

nodes.title: High-Weightage Board Questions & Diagrams
points: Board Diagram 1: T.S. of Testis showing seminiferous tubules, Sertoli cells, spermatogonia, and Leydig cells.
Board Diagram 2: Structure of mature Graafian follicle and unfertilized ovum.
Board Diagram 3: Structure of human sperm (acrosome, head, neck with centrioles, middle piece with mitochondrial spiral/Nebenkern, tail).
Board Diagram 4: Hormonal regulation and changes in endometrium during menstrual cycle (FSH, LH, Estrogen, Progesterone graphs).
Board Distinguish 1: Spermatogenesis vs Oogenesis (equal vs unequal division, continuous vs discontinuous, 4 sperms vs 1 ovum).
Board Distinguish 2: Vasectomy vs Tubectomy.

formulas.label: Pregnancy test detection basis
formulas.expr: Urine hCG detection (secreted by trophoblast cells of blastocyst within days of implantation)

formulas.label: Sperm structure dimensions
formulas.expr: Head (nucleus + acrosome) | Neck (centrioles) | Middle piece (mitochondrial sheath / Nebenkern) | Tail (axial filament)

nodes.title: MHT-CET & NEET High-Speed Shortcuts & Traps
points: TRAP 1: Site of fertilization: Ampulla of Fallopian tube (ampullary-isthmic junction was old NCERT, current official textbook is AMPULLA).
TRAP 2: Secondary oocyte arrest: Ovulation occurs at Metaphase II of Meiosis II. Meiosis II completes ONLY upon sperm entry!
TRAP 3: Hormones unique to pregnancy: hCG, hPL, and Relaxin (in late pregnancy) are produced in women ONLY during pregnancy.
TRAP 4: Copper-T mechanism: Cu²⁺ suppresses sperm motility and fertilizing ability (it does NOT prevent ovulation!).
TRAP 5: Non-steroidal oral pill: Saheli is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (centchroman), taken once a week, zero steroidal side effects (developed by CDRI Lucknow).
TRAP 6: Semen volume & pH: 2.5 - 4.0 mL per ejaculation; alkaline (pH 7.2 - 7.7) to neutralize acidic vaginal environment; normal count 60-120 million/mL.

formulas.label: Pregnancy-exclusive hormones trio
formulas.expr: hCG + hPL + Relaxin (produced exclusively during pregnancy)

formulas.label: Meiotic arrest stages in oogenesis
formulas.expr: Primary oocyte arrested at: Prophase I (Diplotene) | Secondary oocyte arrested at: Metaphase II

formulas.label: Seminal fluid volume and pH
formulas.expr: Ejaculate: 2.5 to 4.0 mL | pH: 7.2 to 7.7 (alkaline) | Sperm count: 60 to 120 million sperms / mL
